title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-04
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains; two newly created repositories found through GitHub Search are appended as discovery signals.
ranking_explanation: Entries 1-13 are ordered by the stars-today values shown on GitHub Trending at snapshot time. Entries 14-15 were created during the last two days and were selected from a GitHub Search scan; no daily Trending delta was available for them, so they are appended and marked N/A.
global_caveat: This is a point-in-time snapshot. Star totals and ranking signals can change. Repository totals, language, and default-branch commits were checked through GitHub REST; Search-discovered entries have no comparable daily star-gain value. No prior-day evidence was gathered, so no shift claim is made.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-04 01:31 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-04 through 2026-11-04. Ranking: daily Trending star gains, with two newly created Search discoveries appended.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-workflow infrastructure leads today's signal: Vercel's agent-desktop gained 3,791 stars, with Scrapling, skills/memory projects, and agent orchestration also drawing strong attention. Local inference and specialized ML remain visible in colibri and Kronos, while a two-day GitHub Search scan surfaced two additional new agent harnesses.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
sections.description: A computer-use CLI that lets agents inspect and operate desktop apps through the operating system's accessibility tree rather than pixel matching.
sections.why_notable: The day's strongest star-gain signal, paired with a concrete, cross-platform agent interaction primitive.
sections.content: A computer-use CLI that exposes desktop UI through accessibility-tree snapshots and element references, rather than pixel matching. The README describes a loop in which the agent observes, acts on refs, and verifies with a fresh snapshot; no model is bundled.

sections.title: D4Vinci/Scrapling
sections.description: A Python scraping framework spanning fast HTTP requests, browser rendering, parsing, and concurrent crawls.
sections.why_notable: One of the day's largest gains; its first-party docs describe reusable sessions, proxy rotation, retries, pause/resume, and agent/MCP access.
sections.content: A Python framework that combines HTTP requests, stealth browsers, parsing, and concurrent crawling. Its README documents reusable sessions, proxy rotation, retries, pause/resume, data exports, and MCP/agent access.

sections.title: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
sections.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.
sections.why_notable: Signals demand for packaged multi-agent workflows applied to a specific production domain.
sections.content: A collection of agents, workflow skills, and coordination rules presented as a game-development studio workflow.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: A collection described by its maintainer as 'Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.'
sections.why_notable: High daily momentum for reusable, task-specific agent instructions rather than a standalone agent product.
sections.content: A repository of agent skills, described by its maintainer as 'Skills for Real Engineers.'

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: A persistent context system that captures tool-use observations, summarizes them, and makes them searchable across sessions.
sections.why_notable: Strong signal for memory and continuity becoming infrastructure around coding agents.
sections.content: A persistent-context system that captures tool-use observations, generates semantic summaries, and makes them available to future sessions. The README describes its MCP search tools and architecture documentation.

sections.title: JustVugg/colibri
sections.description: A C inference engine that runs large mixture-of-experts models by keeping active experts in memory and streaming others from disk.
sections.why_notable: Its RAM/GPU/NVMe hierarchy makes local execution of much larger models the central draw.
sections.content: A pure-C inference engine that serves large MoE models using a hierarchy of RAM-resident hot experts and disk-streamed experts. Its README describes CPU, Vulkan, and CUDA paths and a hardware-aware setup flow.

sections.title: p-e-w/heretic
sections.description: A training-free toolkit for modifying language-model behavior.
sections.why_notable: A distinct model-control theme alongside the broader push toward agent tooling.
sections.content: A training-free language-model modification project; its stated goals include changing censorship, slop, and sycophancy behavior.

sections.title: shiyu-coder/Kronos
sections.description: A family of foundation models and tools for financial-market candlestick sequences.
sections.why_notable: Shows continued interest in domain-specific time-series modeling beyond general-purpose language models.
sections.content: A decoder-only foundation-model family for K-line data, with a specialized tokenizer that discretizes OHLCV sequences and an autoregressive Transformer for downstream quant tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The default branch's last push was 2026-04-13, so its repository activity is much older than today's star-gain signal; README claims are project descriptions, not evidence of predictive performance.

sections.title: floci-io/floci
sections.description: A local emulator for AWS services.
sections.why_notable: A strong infrastructure-testing project among today's application- and agent-heavy trends.
sections.content: A Java-based local emulator positioned as an alternative for testing AWS services without relying on a live AWS environment.

sections.title: max-sixty/worktrunk
sections.description: A Git worktree-management CLI designed for parallel AI-agent workflows.
sections.why_notable: Treats parallel agent work as a repository/workspace management problem, not just a prompting problem.
sections.content: A command-line tool for Git worktree management, specifically designed around parallel AI-agent workflows.

sections.title: anomalyco/hex
sections.description: Local voice dictation software for macOS, Windows, and Linux.
sections.why_notable: Adds a local-first voice input angle to the day's desktop and developer-tool activity.
sections.content: A local dictation application for desktop operating systems, built in Rust.

sections.title: Usagi-org/ai-goofish-monitor
sections.description: A Playwright- and AI-based system for scheduled or live Xianyu marketplace monitoring and analysis.
sections.why_notable: An applied example of task automation and analysis for a specific consumer marketplace.
sections.content: A Playwright- and AI-based monitoring/analysis system for the Xianyu marketplace, described as supporting real-time or scheduled monitoring and a backend UI.
sections.unique_caveat: The default branch's last push was 2026-10-10, predating the snapshot by several weeks.

sections.title: spotify/portal-ai-plugins
sections.description: Spotify's repository for Portal AI plugins.
sections.why_notable: A smaller signal that established developer platforms are also exposing plugin surfaces for AI tooling.
sections.content: A Spotify-owned TypeScript repository named portal-ai-plugins; GitHub provides no repository description.
sections.unique_caveat: GitHub repository description is absent and the default branch was last pushed 2026-10-23, so its precise purpose and current activity are less clear than for the other entries.

sections.title: Balanov/shim
sections.description: A small, local-first Go harness for connecting models, MCP servers, and agent skills through a CLI.
sections.why_notable: A newly created repository found in the last-two-days Search scan; its README emphasizes a single static binary, local configuration, and confirmation for mutating commands.
sections.content: A local-first AI harness described as one static binary with model-provider adapters, MCP and skill support, JSON configuration, and confirmation for mutating commands.
sections.unique_caveat: New Search-discovered repo; GitHub Trending did not provide a daily star-gain value for this entry.

sections.title: KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop
sections.description: A local plugin-based automation layer that dispatches tasks to CLI agents and asks a person to decide when needed.
sections.why_notable: A newly created agent-orchestration project found by GitHub Search; it describes event-driven jobs, resumable work, and human approval for uncertain or risky actions.
sections.content: A plugin-based local automation core that routes scheduled or external events to CLI agents, waits without a continuously running agent process, and resumes after human approval when needed.
sections.unique_caveat: New Search-discovered repo; GitHub Trending did not provide a daily star-gain value for this entry.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflow infrastructure is the broadest shared signal: agent-desktop, claude-mem, worktrunk, skills, game-studio workflows, shim, and agent-autoloop cover interaction, memory, parallelism, and human checkpoints. Colibri and heretic reflect local inference/model control; Scrapling and ai-goofish-monitor emphasize web/data automation; Kronos represents domain-specific financial ML. Languages in the 15 listed repositories: Python 4, Rust 3, TypeScript 3, Shell 2, C 1, Go 1, Java 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest pattern is a shift from standalone assistants toward the infrastructure that makes agents persistent, operable, and coordinated: memory, skills, desktop control, worktrees, and approval loops. Local inference and domain-specific data projects show the trend is broader than coding agents. The two new repositories are Search-discovered additions, not entries with daily Trending star deltas.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary: https://github.com/trending?since=daily. Entries 1-13 are ordered by daily stars-today figures; entries 14-15 are appended Search discoveries with daily gains unavailable. The current total stars, language, and commit SHA are point-in-time GitHub REST values. No prior-day comparison was available.
